draft.title: The Victorian Law Reform Commission
card: The Victorian Law Reform Commission (VLRC) is an independent body that researches the law and suggests how to improve it. It is set up by an Act of the Victorian Parliament.
It usually works on a reference. This is a topic that the Attorney-General sends to it for review. It can also take on some work of its own, but referrals are its main source.
The VLRC studies the current law, reads other places' laws and asks the public for views through consultation. It then writes a report with recommendations.
The VLRC cannot make or change laws. Parliament decides whether to act on the report. Governments often accept recommendations, but they do not have to.
draft.remember: The VLRC researches and recommends. Parliament decides.

a.q: What is the main role of the VLRC in law reform?
opts: To research a referred issue and recommend changes
To pass a law once it has finished its research
To hear appeals about laws that are unfair
To order the government to adopt its reports
a.why: The VLRC investigates an issue sent to it and reports with recommendations. It cannot pass laws or order change, because only Parliament can make law. Passing a law is the most tempting wrong option, but it confuses a recommending body with a law-making one.
a.clue: Think about who has the power to make law.

b.q: The Attorney-General refers a topic to the VLRC. After public consultation, the VLRC reports, but Parliament does not act on every recommendation. What does this show?
opts: The VLRC advises, and Parliament chooses what to adopt
The VLRC failed, because its reports must become law
The VLRC is not independent, as it acts on a referral
The VLRC can pass its own laws if Parliament delays
b.why: The VLRC's role is to recommend, so Parliament may adopt some, all or none of its advice. A referral does not remove its independence, because the VLRC still researches and reaches its own conclusions. The option about failure is tempting but wrongly treats reports as binding.
b.clue: Who holds the power to make the final decision?

a.best: To research a referred issue and recommend changes

b.best: The VLRC advises, and Parliament chooses what to adopt

problems.detail: Why (a) says 'only Parliament can make law'. In VCE Legal Studies, courts also make law through common law (point 3 of this chapter), so this teaches something false. It should say that the VLRC cannot make law and that Parliament decides whether to act on its recommendations.
The chapter point says a recent inquiry shows how much the VLRC can achieve, but the card names no inquiry and gives no example of what it achieved.

proposal.title: The Victorian Law Reform Commission

It mainly works on references: topics the Attorney-General sends it to review. It studies the current law, looks at other places' laws and asks the public for views, then writes a report with recommendations.
The VLRC cannot make or change laws. Parliament decides whether to act on its report. Governments often accept recommendations, but they do not have to.
Example: in 2021 the VLRC reported on how the justice system responds to sexual offences. In 2022 Parliament acted on many of its recommendations, including changes to how consent is defined.
